Subject: Zenith RFI - inference stress/soak validation and throughput/latency metrics

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this RFI. As part of our vendor validation for the inference layer we need a concise, reproducible test plan that demonstrates:
- 95th/99th percentile latencies at varying concurrencies (1, 4, 16, 64)
- Sustained throughput for 1hr, 6hr soak, and 24hr soak under typical and peak traffic patterns
- CPU/GPU utilization profiles and memory/KV cache behavior during warm and cold cache tests
- Failure/recovery behavior (node preemption, transient network loss) and automatic fallback characteristics

Can Redwood provide: the test methodology, artifacts/scripts, example results (for a 13B and a 70B model), and any assumptions about batching, quantization, and model variants? Also please include any constraints when tests are run in our Azure VNet vs Redwood hosted environment.

Subject: RE: Zenith RFI - inference stress/soak validation and throughput/latency metrics

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear ask. We've put together a reproducible "Stress + Soak" validation we run for enterprise RFPs; summary attached and core details below. We'll include runnable load scripts (k6 and Locust), a CSV test matrix, and example dashboards from prior runs on both hosted and dedicated capacity.

Summary of deliverables (attached: redwood-stress-soak-protocol-v2.pdf):
- Test phases: cold-start microbench (single-request latency), steady-state concurrency sweep (1/4/16/64), burst/pulse tests (3x baseline for 60s), 1hr soak, 6hr soak, 24hr soak.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model throughput (tokens/s per GPU), request CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, memory peaks, error rates, and tail latency distribution.
- Failure injection: node termination, simulated 250ms network blackhole, and model process restart; we capture failover times and routing fallback-to-compatible-variant behavior.
- Assumptions & config: batching max_tokens=1024, dynamic batching windows tuned per concurrency, typical tokenizer length = 128 tokens, quantized variants used for throughput baselines with reported quality delta.
- Environment notes: For Azure VNet runs we recommend colocated worker subnets with a throughput-optimized NIC; tests that require root-level telemetry need a short-running agent (we provide an agent container). Hosted runs use our dedicated test cluster with identical kernel/driver stack where possible.
- Example results: included are anonymized 13B and 70B sample runs (summary tables) and a recommended observability dashboard.

Timeline: we can deliver the protocol and initial sample results by COB Monday if we have a short call to confirm target model variants and whether you want the run inside your VNet or on Redwood-hosted test infra.

Notes: attaching the protocol + initial test matrix; will follow up with load scripts and a proposed 90-min test window.

Best,
